newsitem.title: USA: ADRs surge on Fed rate hike, then ease.
newsitem.headline: ADRs surge on Fed rate hike, then ease.

text.p: Foreign companies' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) eased on Tuesday after an initial jump on higher U.S. interest rates, traders said.
"It's kind of mixed at the moment, they are basically following the Dow," a trader in European ADRs said.
The Dow industrials' had briefly surged then fell back on the Federal Reserve's announcement it would increase the rate on federal funds to 5.5 from 5.25 percent, or 25 basis points.
"Nobody knows what the heck to do right now. ... People can't decide whether to buy or sell," the trader said.
Among European ADRs, Swedish telephone equipment maker LM Ericsson rose 1/4 to 33-3/4 and was among the most-active ADRs.
ADRs in Telefonos de Mexico, the most heavily traded foreign share, fell 1/8 to 38-3/4. Brazilian bellwether Telebras fell 3/4 to 106-3/4.

Most analysts said they expected Latin American equities to drop briefly after the rate hike and then rally as investors sought bargains. Latin American stocks historically are sensitive to U.S. interest rate changes.
Stefano Natella, a Latin American analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, said in a report, "If the Federal Reserve implements at 25 basis point tightening, buy immediately."

He added, "Fed tightening is bullish for Latin equities as it should reduce uncertainty and return investor focus to both strong fundamentals and wide interest rate differentials between U.S. and local rates."

Decliners barely outpaced advancers 258 to 257 in late afternoon trade among 806 ADRS. The ADR index was up 0.18 percent after rising about 0.27 percent just after the Fed increase, and volume was 50 million shares.
